author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of a pure mind and simple intention

verses.text: By two wings is man lifted above earthly things, even by simplicity and purity.
verses.modernizedText: By two wings a person is lifted above earthly things: simplicity and purity.

verses.text: Simplicity ought to be in the intention, purity in the affection.
verses.modernizedText: Simplicity ought to be in the intention, purity in the affection.

verses.text: Simplicity reacheth towards God, purity apprehendeth Him and tasteth Him.
verses.modernizedText: Simplicity reaches toward God; purity grasps Him and tastes Him.

verses.text: No good action will be distasteful to thee if thou be free within from inordinate affection.
verses.modernizedText: No good action will be distasteful to you if you are free within from excessive affection.

verses.text: If thou reachest after and seekest, nothing but the will of God and the benefit of thy neighbour, thou wilt entirely enjoy inward liberty.
verses.modernizedText: If you reach after and seek nothing but the will of God and the benefit of your neighbor, you will entirely enjoy inward liberty.

verses.text: If thine heart were right, then should every creature be a mirror of life and a book of holy doctrine.
verses.modernizedText: If your heart were right, then every creature would be a mirror of life and a book of holy doctrine.

verses.text: There is no creature so small and vile but that it showeth us the goodness of God.
verses.modernizedText: There is no creature so small and lowly that it does not show us the goodness of God.

verses.text: If thou wert good and pure within, then wouldst thou look upon all things without hurt and understand them aright.
verses.modernizedText: If you were good and pure within, then you would look upon all things without harm and understand them rightly.

verses.text: A pure heart seeth the very depths of heaven and hell.
verses.modernizedText: A pure heart sees the very depths of heaven and hell.

verses.text: Such as each one is inwardly, so judgeth he outwardly.
verses.modernizedText: As each person is inwardly, so he judges outwardly.

verses.text: If there is any joy in the world surely the man of pure heart possesseth it, and if there is anywhere tribulation and anguish, the evil conscience knoweth it best.
verses.modernizedText: If there is any joy in the world, surely the person of pure heart possesses it; and if there is tribulation and anguish anywhere, the evil conscience knows it best.

verses.text: As iron cast into the fire loseth rust and is made altogether glowing, so the man who turneth himself altogether unto God is freed from slothfulness and changed into a new man.
verses.modernizedText: As iron cast into the fire loses rust and is made altogether glowing, so the person who turns himself entirely to God is freed from sloth and changed into a new person.

verses.text: When a man beginneth to grow lukewarm, then he feareth a little labour, and willingly accepteth outward consolation; but when he beginneth perfectly to conquer himself and to walk manfully in the way of God, then he counteth as nothing those things which aforetime seemed to be so grievous unto him.
verses.modernizedText: When a person begins to grow lukewarm, he fears a little labor and willingly accepts outward consolation; but when he begins completely to conquer himself and walk courageously in the way of God, he counts as nothing those things that formerly seemed so grievous to him.
